title: Accessible micro-viewport controls and tooltip buffering for ultra-high-density time series
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Our current time-series components exhibit poor UX for ultra-high-density traces (hundreds+ series or samples per pixel): tooltips flicker during fast mouse moves, keyboard focus jumps are noisy for screen readers, and the DOM-heavy tooltip implementations cause CPU spikes in dashboards with many concurrent charts. This ticket defines a design and interaction spec to introduce a lightweight micro-viewport control and a tooltip buffering strategy that reduces visual noise, improves accessibility, and cuts client CPU during heavy workloads.

Goals:
- Provide precise focus/selection without showing full tooltips for every mouse micro-movement.
- Ensure screen readers receive concise, meaningful summaries instead of a stream of single-data-point announcements.
- Reduce tooltip DOM churn and rendering cost while preserving discoverability on hover/tap.
- Smooth keyboard navigation across dense series and keep a single accessible announcer for updates.

Proposed solution summary:
1) Micro-viewport control: a composable, minimal control that appears on hover or keyboard focus near the cursor or keyboard focus ring. It shows a condensed set of actions: pin point, open expanded detail, and toggle series highlight. On mobile it appears under long-press as a compact sheet. The control is primarily canvas-driven for visuals with a single accessible DOM node used for interaction and aria attributes.
2) Tooltip buffering (debounce + sample): instead of rendering a tooltip for every movement, buffer updates for 80-150ms and coalesce multiple events into one rendered summary. For sustained hovers show progressive disclosure: first a micro-summary (value/series name), then a richer popup after a longer dwell.
3) Screen-reader friendly summary: maintain an aria-live="polite" offscreen summary node that emits compact summaries (series count, min/max in viewport, time range) rather than every point. Provide a keyboard action to read expanded details.
4) Performance optimizations: move visual indicator rendering to canvas layers with an offscreen cache for recent samples, use rAF batching for hover updates, and implement a DOM pool for tooltip nodes to avoid repeated create/destroy cycles. Provide a decimation fallback that reduces rendered sample density when CPU/paint cost crosses thresholds.
5) The design tokens and focus treatment will reuse the system color tokens but introduces a new focus-style token for tiny interactive overlays to keep contrast and reduce visual clutter.

Trade-offs considered:
- Buffer delay improves stability but increases time-to-first-detail; mitigated by a two-stage disclosure pattern.
- Canvas-first visuals mean less semantic HTML for individual points; compensated by a robust offscreen aria summary and explicit keyboard affordances.
- Decimation reduces fidelity under load; policy will be conservative and documented so downstream consumers can opt-in/out at route-level.

Deliverables:
- Figma spec for micro-viewport controls and keyboard flows (desktop & mobile).
- Interaction spec doc with timing thresholds and accessibility text snippets.
- Visual tokens diff for focus-overlay and tooltip micro-variant.
- Prototype branch with lightweight JS/Canvas proof-of-concept and a small benchmark harness.
acceptance_criteria: Figma mockups linked and approved by design and PM (desktop, tablet, mobile)
Interaction spec published with explicit timing: micro-summary delay, expanded-popup dwell, and keyboard focus behaviour
ARIA strategy documented and validated: aria-live summary exists and reads concise summaries rather than every point
Performance targets verified in prototype: tooltip-related CPU at 95th percentile reduced by >=35% on a 1000-series synthetic load
Keyboard-only navigation passes WCAG 2.1 AA for focus order and visible focus indicators
E2E test added that asserts micro-viewport appears and expands only after configured dwell time
Design tokens for focus-overlay and tooltip micro-variant added to the design system token file and referenced in spec
